criteria.prompt: Original/permitted source, author, distribution rights and no learner PII checked.
criteria.evidence: Astra: Provenance identifies the Dual Dictionary project, original AI-assisted reading and an explicit original-source rights statement. All three source sentences concern fictional researchers, generic transport choices and a council; no learner personal data or externally attributed text is present. Rights are accepted on the project declaration, not independently certified authorship. criteria.prompt: Phrase occurs in cited source and the contextual sense is supported.
criteria.evidence: Astra: Carry out a survey appears verbatim in s1. Researchers collecting information about transport choices supports the conduct-a-survey sense. Terra: s1 contains carry out a survey about transport choices.

criteria.prompt: English gloss is the actual contextual meaning, not a selection rationale.
criteria.evidence: Astra: The EN gloss accurately describes conducting this information-gathering survey through questions. Contextual wording does not claim that all technical surveys use questionnaires. Terra: Conducting a question-based survey to collect information is appropriate to this context, though the source does not specify a method.

criteria.prompt: Vietnamese gloss is accurate, natural and includes diacritics.

criteria.prompt: Phrase occurs in cited source and the contextual sense is supported.
criteria.evidence: Astra: Draw a distinction between appears verbatim in s2, introducing occasional visitors and daily work travelers as different groups. Terra: s2 contains draw a distinction between visitors and people commuting daily.

criteria.prompt: English gloss is the actual contextual meaning, not a selection rationale.
criteria.evidence: Astra: The EN gloss correctly expresses recognizing/showing a difference between things and fits the grouping in s2. Terra: Recognizing and showing a difference captures the distinction in context.

criteria.prompt: Vietnamese gloss is accurate, natural and includes diacritics.
criteria.evidence: Astra: Chỉ ra sự khác biệt giữa is accurate, natural Vietnamese for showing a distinction between the groups. q3c repeats it consistently. Terra: Chỉ ra sự khác biệt giữa naturally expresses showing the difference between groups.

criteria.prompt: Identify correct option and explain each distractor. No other plausible answer; no subjective style/intent assumptions.
criteria.evidence: Astra: q1: b alone gives the meaning of conducting the survey. a describes inspecting final results after completion; that is not what the phrase means. c describes cancellation and is incompatible with conducting as a meaning. Each choice was read independently. Terra: b defines conducting the survey; a describes later examination of results and c cancellation, neither defines conducting.

criteria.prompt: Every option explanation is accurate; grammar/collocation claims are not overgeneralized.
criteria.evidence: Astra: q1a correctly distinguishes later final-result inspection from information collection; q1b explains collection by questions; revised q1c accurately contrasts cancellation with conducting without requiring an already-completed result. The overall explanation correctly selects b. Terra: All explanations distinguish doing, reviewing results and cancelling; asking questions is a reasonable contextual interpretation, not a method stated explicitly in the source.

criteria.prompt: Identify correct option and explain each distractor. No other plausible answer; no subjective style/intent assumptions.
criteria.evidence: Astra: q2: a naturally uses carried out a survey about lunch choices. b has the unsuitable topic preposition in lunch choices, repaired with about/on. c omits the determiner required for singular count survey in this full sentence. Only a is defensible. Terra: a is idiomatic; b uses in with lunch choices where about/on is appropriate; c lacks a determiner for singular survey.

criteria.prompt: Every option explanation is accurate; grammar/collocation claims are not overgeneralized.
criteria.evidence: Astra: q2a correctly endorses the collocation; q2b allows both about and on and makes no exclusive-about rule; q2c supplies a valid minimal article repair. The overall explanation matches all options. Terra: a describes correct collocation; b supplies appropriate about/on, c supplies a; summary correctly identifies a.

criteria.prompt: Identify correct option and explain each distractor. No other plausible answer; no subjective style/intent assumptions.
criteria.evidence: Astra: q3: c gives recognizing/showing differences. a reverses the meaning by ignoring differences. b describes an invitation to travel together, which is a different act even though distinguished groups could also share a bus. Only c defines the phrase. Terra: c defines distinguishing; a ignores differences and b invites people to share a bus, neither defines the phrase.

criteria.prompt: Every option explanation is accurate; grammar/collocation claims are not overgeneralized.
criteria.evidence: Astra: q3a accurately identifies the opposite sense; q3b rejects the invitation as a definition without claiming shared travel is impossible; revised q3c uses the source-appropriate label daily commuters and consistent Vietnamese. Overall explanation matches c. Terra: All three explanations and summary correctly contrast the choices; the Vietnamese gloss matches the contextual meaning.

criteria.prompt: Identify correct option and explain each distractor. No other plausible answer; no subjective style/intent assumptions.
criteria.evidence: Astra: q4: b has draws a distinction between A and B. a wrongly connects the two intended comparison groups with to instead of and; c omits a from draw a distinction in the standard full sentence. Only b expresses the required comparison naturally. Terra: b uses the natural between A and B pattern; a uses to instead of and, c lacks a determiner before singular distinction.

criteria.prompt: Every option explanation is accurate; grammar/collocation claims are not overgeneralized.
criteria.evidence: Astra: q4a identifies the between A and B structure; q4b confirms its two noun phrases and collocation; q4c supplies the missing a. The overall explanation is consistent. These are grammatical/collocational judgments, not judgments that one topic is too trivial or a speaker too informal. criteria.prompt: Role or purpose differs meaningfully from the source; not merely rewriting it.
criteria.evidence: Astra: Transfer changes researchers explaining transport categories into a student helping a classmate understand two library book categories and borrowing rules. Both audience and communicative purpose change materially. Terra: Explaining school-library borrowing rules to a classmate changes role, audience and purpose from a transport survey.

The invented two-week loan is plausible within the fictional situation. Formal phrasing remains compatible with a helpful classmate message. Each checklist entry is observable: exact phrase, two items plus difference, 2–3 sentences and helpful tone. No automatic grading is asserted. Checklist covers phrase, contrast and audience/length; no automatic grade.

options.text: to look at the final results after a survey is finished
options.explanation: This is wrong because looking at results happens after collecting information, while the sentence describes collecting information by asking questions.

options.text: to conduct a survey by asking people questions to collect information
options.explanation: This is correct because it matches asking people questions to collect information about transport (tiến hành một cuộc khảo sát).

options.text: to cancel a survey because people do not want to answer
options.explanation: Wrong: Cancelling means stopping or deciding not to conduct a survey; carrying out a survey means conducting it.
